title: Bounded-degree coboundary expanders in every dimension
coverage:
I read the whole LaTeX source: introduction, construction, geometry, homology, expansion and the figure. Checks made:
(1) Lemma 2.1 (local group patterns). I re-derived the block structure of H_i by hand, block-diagonal unitriangular blocks with a kt lower-left block, and confirmed that these matrices form a group of order q^{C(N,2)}. I also confirmed by brute force that the generators x_j produce groups of exactly this order modulo t^2 (N=3,4, q=3). The intersection identities and injectivity of reduction for m>=2 hold.
(2) Lattice stabilizers. The bounds deg g_ab <= b_a - b_b at the chosen vertices give exactly H_0 and H_i. The intersection over the chamber is B_-, so the chamber is opposite c_+, and U acts simply transitively because B_+ = U⋊T and B_+∩B_- = T.
(3) Codistance filtration. The descent set, the residue and c_max argument, the attaching locus ∂F*O, the relative chains formula and the degree range k < |D|+|J|-1 = n are all correct. This gives reduced homology of L vanishing for j < n-1.
(4) Partial projective resolution lemma, the U-orbit complex being a single simplex, and Γ_N(m)\L ≅ T_m with free action. All correct.
(5) Stabilization. Γ_a(m) = GL_a(t^m k[t]). The relative stable-range verification is correct. The universal coefficient step uses only integral degrees j and j-1, which are both in range. Transfer has odd (q-power) index, so the transition maps are surjective, and a pro-zero system with surjective transitions is zero.
(6) Trivial action. N-2 = 2(d-1)+1 meets the range for two stabilization steps. e_ab(f) centralizes the congruence block on the complementary coordinates, which I checked by direct matrix computation. The odd-order coinvariant / LHS argument then gives H_j(Γ_N(m)) = H_j(U) = 0 for 1 <= j <= d-1.
(7) Weight comparison. I checked ν_s = Λμ_s/c, and the averaging identity via C(n+1,s+1)C(s+1,i+1) = C(n+1,i+1)C(n-i,s-i). Λ cancels and ε = η/M. The vertex-degree bound and the growth estimate are correct.
Not checked: the exact statements of the cited theorems. These are the Iwasa Thm 5.13 range a >= 2j+r-1 for pro-isomorphism, OVB Cor 6.10 (opposition complexes are acyclic for q >= 2^{r-1}; this agrees with the type-A bound I recall from Abramenko), OVB Thm 1.2 and its KMS-complex definition, and Morrow Thm 0.3. The argument only needs surjectivity in degree j plus an isomorphism in degree j-1, so a one-off difference in Iwasa's range would still be fine unless the surjectivity range itself is weaker.
main_claim: For every d>=3 there are arbitrarily large connected pure d-dimensional complexes X_m with bounded vertex degree and uniform F_2 coboundary expansion in all degrees i<d. X_m is the d-skeleton of the congruence KMS coset complex of U ≤ SL_{2d+1}(F_q[t]) modulo t^m. Expansion comes from the OVB cosystolic expansion theorem combined with cohomology vanishing proved via twin-building acyclicity and homology pro-stability.
sibling_notes: Family 177 board was empty at audit time. Lemmas that could be reused: odd-index transfer turns a pro-zero cokernel into level-wise zero; two stabilization steps give trivial conjugation action on H_j(Γ_N(m);F_2).
